clue.text: Bumbling thieves net a small fraction of whole

definitions.note: one of seventy equal parts into which a whole is divided

indicators.note: bumbling means clumsy and confused, so the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Clumsy burglars bag only a tiny share of the haul.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinal fraction: one part in seventy is a small portion of a whole.

clue.text: Ready to show regret, over and over

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to rue is to show regret
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Someone poised to apologise again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is British slang for cash ('the ready'), and the euro is a currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for money in hand; a European currency unit is a form of such cash.

clue.text: Bury's centre wiped out in dreadful bombardment

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
the middle five letters of the word bombardment are removed, leaving its two ends

explanation.surface: A town called Bury has its middle flattened by a terrible air raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre wiped out in' removes BARDM from BOMBARDMENT, leaving BOMENT; 'dreadful' rearranges it. Bury is also a Lancashire town, which is the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: to bury a body is to place it in a tomb.

clue.text: Boozed very quietly, wearing hat, and finally snoozed

indicators.note: the hat word is worn around the quiet letters, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quietly

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of snoozed

explanation.surface: A drinker sips quietly in a hat and then nods off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tile' for a hat is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to tipple is to drink alcohol habitually, so the past tense means drank.

clue.text: Serve up fabricated dairy product

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom, read upwards

parts.note: something fabricated has been made

explanation.surface: Dish out a manufactured cheese or yoghurt.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Dutch cheese is a product of the dairy.

clue.text: Doctor seen in unusually rough headwear

indicators.note: the doctor's letters are seen inside the rearranged word
unusually says the letters of rough are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A medic turns up in a strangely rough-looking hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a felt hat with a dented crown, named after a German spa town.

clue.text: Type of 28 caught nothing before stoppage

definitions.note: the cross-reference points to the answer at 28 across, a tied loop of rope

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
love is zero in tennis scoring
a hitch is a hold-up or stoppage

explanation.surface: A cricket scorecard: a catch, a duck, then play halted.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a sailor's hitch made with two turns around a post is one kind of tied loop.

clue.text: Daily appeal's skilful and generous

parts.note: a daily, or char, is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
it is old slang for sex appeal
able means capable or skilful

explanation.surface: A newspaper's fundraising campaign is clever and open-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in Britain a daily or char is a cleaner. 'It' for sex appeal is old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a charitable person is kind and liberal in giving.

clue.text: Black Prince has returned? That's bunkum!

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: returned means the name is turned back to front

parts.note: Hal is Shakespeare's Prince Henry

explanation.surface: Has the Black Prince come back? Rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both words mean empty talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Basis of life found in most of apple roots scattered on motorway

indicators.note: scattered says the letters are strewn into a new order
most of says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a British motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Fruit-tree roots strewn on a motorway turn out to hold the secret of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final E; 'scattered' then rearranges the nine letters, giving PROTOPLAS before the motorway letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A biology term: the living material of a cell is the physical foundation of life.

clue.text: Two verses penned by 'Old Dutch of East London' perhaps giving trouble in Hackney

indicators.note: the two verse letters are penned, or enclosed, by the Dutch word

parts.note: a Boer is a South African of old Dutch stock
V is the abbreviation for verse, so two of them give VV

explanation.surface: A Cockney wife ("my old Dutch") writes some verses that cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife, the false picture. Hackney is an East London borough; bovver is Cockney for aggro or trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialect: a Cockney pronunciation of a word for bother, meaning street violence or aggro.

clue.text: Fats changes first line to R 'n' B for songster

indicators.note: changes first says the first of the line letters is swapped for another piece

parts.note: Fats Waller was the American jazz pianist and singer
rhythm and blues is abbreviated RB

explanation.surface: Fats Waller's style shifts to rhythm and blues.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' marks what the first L becomes. The answer is also the setter's pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small bird known for its song is a songster.

clue.text: War king surrounds forlorn tower at start of siege bringing much weeping

indicators.note: the war king pair surrounds the shuffled tower, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: forlorn, in a sorry state, signals the letters of tower are rearranged
at start of picks out the opening letter of siege

explanation.surface: A warlord rings a desolate tower as a siege begins, causing tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn on the waterworks' is a British idiom for crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a flood of tears is jokingly called this, as if from a water supply system.

clue.text: What should be considered if rock star breaks down

indicators.note: breaks down signals the letters collapse and are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: A rock star's breakdown is something to weigh up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a condition that raises the chance of harm is something that must be taken into account.

clue.text: Tree is giant. It regularly produces sap

indicators.note: regularly picks out every second letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: A huge tree that oozes sap regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosely a synonym: the sticky substance trees exude is a kind of tree sap.

clue.text: Reptile that man caught at last, working with hook and loops

parts.note: croc is short for crocodile
he is the pronoun for that man

indicators.note: at last picks out the closing letter of caught

explanation.surface: A crocodile hunter finally lands his catch with a hook and a noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft term: needlework done with a hooked needle that pulls yarn through loops.

clue.text: Weight of vehicle? One ton

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a means one

explanation.surface: How heavy is the vehicle? A ton.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit: the measure of mass for gemstones, 200 milligrams.

clue.text: As a prank remove pants from some rude baggage

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Pranksters steal the trousers from an ill-mannered person's luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to pull someone's trousers off as a joke, a student prank.

clue.text: Chum's 9

definitions.meaning: a British form of address to a man, like mate or pal
the cross-reference points to the answer at 9 across, meaning nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a casual British address for a stranger, and slang for rubbish talk.

clue.text: Fag end is beginning to smoulder on boat

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of smoulder

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A cigarette butt starts to smoulder on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the short remaining stump of a smoked cigarette.

clue.text: Great artist one's ignored

indicators.note: one is ignored, so the letter for one is dropped from the artist's name

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A great painter is overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great artist' reads as one phrase, but 'Great' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: something titanic or colossal; the word is used attributively for anything huge.

clue.text: It's upsetting, daughter in strongly regarded clothes treated thus?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the word upside down so it reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the daughter letter goes in the looked-at word

parts.note: eyed means looked at closely

explanation.surface: An upset daughter in garish clothes is stared at.
explanation.definitionFit: A craft process: fabric knotted and dipped in colour so the tied parts resist the dye.

clue.text: So-called 'lion man' falls to pieces

indicators.note: falls to pieces signals the letters break apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: A supposed lion man collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: in name only, existing as a label rather than in fact.

clue.text: Hold back from putting a fire out in outskirts of Rouen

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in between the outer letters
outskirts of picks out the first and last letters of Rouen
out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Firefighters on the edge of Rouen hold off from tackling a blaze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A FIRE to EFRAI, set between R and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to refrain is to abstain or restrain oneself from doing something.

clue.text: Gout's boiling hot — that is becoming a difficult problem

indicators.note: boiling signals the letters of gout are churned up

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ie, id est, is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A painful, inflamed gout becomes a hard case to treat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is also the name of this Telegraph puzzle series.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal: a hard nut to crack, a puzzle or task that takes effort.

clue.text: Flyer's energy starts to dwindle with increased travel

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A bird's stamina begins to fade on long flights.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a long-billed wading bird is a creature that flies.

clue.text: No time to burn papers in plant

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: to torch is to set on fire
ID stands for identity papers

explanation.surface: Not a moment to burn documents in the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' could be a factory, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: an exotic flowering species is a plant.

clue.text: Copper runs back to grab restraint

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: back to picks out the closing letter of grab

explanation.surface: A policeman races back to seize a culprit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a check or control that holds something in.

clue.text: Photo's ruined

definitions.meaning: worn out or wrecked, as in 'my nerves are gone'

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a camera snap, and informal for wrecked or worn out.

clue.text: Mentioning no names, old women will seek admission to woo hunky criminal

indicators.note: the old women letters are admitted inside the shuffled phrase
criminal says the letters of the phrase are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: Elderly ladies queue to court a handsome villain, discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges WOO HUNKY to YOUKNWHO, and O plus W go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a phrase used to refer to someone without saying who, deliberately avoiding names.

clue.text: Ravel, that has a negative effect for the listener

indicators.note: for the listener says the word is heard, not written

parts.note: not is a word of negation

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel, whose music sounds bad to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer, but it means tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to ravel is to entangle, and a tangle is a twisted loop.

clue.text: Weaken European power essentially in specified time

indicators.note: the European and power pieces go in the time word

parts.note: a date is a specified time

indicators.note: essentially keeps only the core, so the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: ability is power or capacity

explanation.surface: European power erodes at a set moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to make feeble or sap the strength of something.
